profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the consortium's applied ML workstream and the platform integration workstream for an internal dry run of a federated graph learning demo aimed at cross-bank financial crime detection. Three participating banks have already contributed approved synthetic or masked data slices into the shared program, and both teams already have access to the sandbox and the secure pre-production enclave. The immediate need is to align the Friday handoff from ML to integration so Daniel's team can prepare Monday's end-to-end dry run and the sponsor-facing rehearsal later that week. The agenda is to confirm what artifacts and configs will be delivered, which prior benchmark the dashboard will compare against, which environment is the assumed target for the dry run, and what each side means by the flow being demo-ready. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on timing, interfaces, shared artifacts, and the execution plan, without reopening governance or architecture decisions.

members.name: Aisha Rahman
members.expertise: Cross-institution ML delivery, model governance coordination, AML analytics translation, stakeholder demos
members.background: Aisha works in the innovation office of a large retail bank and coordinates the consortium's data science workstream; she previously led sanctions screening modernization efforts and now focuses on turning research outputs into sponsor-friendly demonstrations across bank partners.
members.private_state: She wants the dry run to feel polished for senior sponsors while minimizing any last-minute packaging work from the data science team, which is already stretched; she is also quietly trying to avoid surfacing operational questions that could turn a straightforward demo rehearsal into a governance review.
hidden_assumptions: When everyone says 'the baseline,' they mean the latest local-only benchmark her ML team has been using in recent January review decks on the FCA TechSprint-derived graph slice.

If Daniel asks for 'model artifacts and configs,' he is asking for the same practical handoff her scientists already exchange internally: exported weights, feature mapping files, run parameters, and a short README.
For this specific demo, 'the demo environment' naturally means the lighter sandbox stack both teams already use for screenshots, quick reruns, and reduced-volume graph execution.
Because both teams already have access to both environments, there is no need to restate which one is intended unless someone explicitly wants to switch.
A flow is 'demo-ready' once the story can be shown end-to-end with stable visuals and uplift numbers, even if a couple of setup steps are still done manually by the ML team off-screen.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Secure data platforms, regulated deployment workflows, MLOps integration, audit-ready execution
members.background: Daniel leads engineering integration for the consortium's technology vendor and has spent six years implementing controlled model and data handoffs for banks and public-private analytics programs in tightly governed environments.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the integration path aligned with the platform's standard operating model and avoid creating one-off exceptions that undermine repeatability; he is also under pressure to show that the federated platform can support operationally credible execution, not just a research prototype.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to 'the baseline,' they mean the approved December steering-pack benchmark already reflected in the dashboard template: the transaction-only local model used as the program's common comparator.

If Aisha says she will send 'model artifacts and configs,' she means the standard deployable bundle their teams have used before: the versioned container reference, manifest, schema contract, and execution config that tell the platform what to run.

For this specific demo, 'the demo environment' defaults to the secure pre-production enclave because that is where federation orchestration, participant separation, and audit logging actually behave like the real platform.
Since both teams already have credentials to both environments, there is no operational need to discuss access or connection details in a short coordination meeting.
A flow is 'demo-ready' only when it can be launched from the orchestrator with complete metadata and rerun without ad hoc notebook intervention.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the baseline' and discuss showing uplift against it in the demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the most recent local-only benchmark produced by the ML team in January on the latest FCA TechSprint-derived graph slice, which includes refreshed local feature engineering and is the comparison currently used in internal ML reviews.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the older approved benchmark from the December steering materials, a transaction-only local model already embedded in the dashboard structure and governance narrative.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have a legitimate, widely recognized artifact known internally as 'the baseline,' and because the meeting is about coordination rather than model methodology, the phrase feels settled enough that neither thinks to qualify which benchmark object they mean.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'model artifacts and configs'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Aisha will send 'the model artifacts and configs' by Friday for Daniel to wire into the run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means the trained weights file, feature mapping outputs, JSON run parameters, and a concise README that lets the integration team reproduce the already-prepared demo flow with light ML assistance if needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the standard deployable bundle implied by prior platform handoffs: container reference or packaged runtime, manifest, schema contract, and execution config that the orchestrator can invoke without bespoke interpretation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Unlike asking whether the model is containerized outright, 'artifacts and configs' sounds like a routine handoff phrase that each side already uses within its own workflow; the missing pieces are second-order packaging assumptions that feel obviously bundled into the phrase, so neither enumerates them.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on making the flow 'demo-ready' for the dry run next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'demo-ready' to mean the audience can see a smooth end-to-end federated learning story with uplift, graph views, and no visible glitches, even if some backstage setup or parameter loading is done manually by her team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'demo-ready' to mean the workflow runs from the orchestrator with complete audit metadata, reproducible execution, and no dependence on manual notebook steps outside the approved platform path.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase functions as harmless schedule shorthand, and both members are sincerely trying to support the same dry run date; the divergent completion standards stay hidden because surface agreement on readiness and timing sounds sufficient in a coordination call.

misalignment_points.topic: Which environment is the default target for this demo
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss running the dry run in 'the demo environment' before the sponsor session.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the sandbox demo stack both teams already use for quick turnaround, reduced graph volume, and polished screenshots, and she assumes that is the natural target for this particular rehearsal unless someone says otherwise.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the secure pre-production federated enclave that both teams can already access, where orchestration, participant isolation, and audit trails are enabled, and he assumes that is the natural target for any serious end-to-end dry run.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The subtlety comes from the fact that both already have access to both environments, so there is no practical reason to discuss credentials, endpoints, or provisioning; each side simply defaults to a different environment for 'this demo,' making the phrase sound unambiguous while masking the divergence.
